title: DECO: Decoupled Multimodal Diffusion Transformer for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation with a Plugin Tactile Adapter
claim: A multi-part policy decouples each input modality into its own conditioning pathway, supported by a large multi-scenario dataset.
layout: Central rounded architecture diagram over a surrounding mosaic of dataset frames; flows top to bottom
description: A large rounded white panel in the center holds the DECO architecture, with the title 'DECO' at upper left. Three input streams enter from the top and sides. Binocular images go through an image encoder, and noisy actions go through an action encoder. Their tokens are concatenated, shown as yellow and gray squares joined by a double arrow. Proprioceptive states and an optional task-level condition pass through linear encoders into an AdaLN block, drawn in green and purple on the left. Tactile signals from a hand icon pass through a tactile encoder into orange tokens and a cross-attention bar on the right. A purple stack of Adapter plus MMDiT Block layers sits in the middle. Denoised action tokens, in green, come out at the bottom. Around the panel, tinted grids of robot camera frames in blue, orange, green and lavender show the four dataset scenarios.
caption: Overview of the Proposed DECO Framework. DECO is a DiT-based policy that decouples multimodal conditioning. Image and action tokens interact via joint self attention, while proprioceptive states and optional conditions are injected through adaptive layer normalization. Tactile signals are injected via cross attention, while a lightweight LoRA-based adapter is used to efficiently fine-tune the pretrained policy. DECO is also accompanied by DECO-50, a bimanual dexterous manipulation dataset with tactile sensing, consisting of 4 scenarios and 28 sub-tasks, covering more than 50 hours of data, approximately 5 million frames, and 8,000 successful trajectories.
abstract: Bimanual dexterous manipulation relies on integrating multimodal inputs to perform complex real-world tasks. To address the challenges of effectively combining these modalities, we propose DECO, a decoupled multimodal diffusion transformer that disentangles vision, proprioception, and tactile signals through specialized conditioning pathways, enabling structured and controllable integration of multimodal inputs, with a lightweight adapter for parameter-efficient injection of additional signals. Alongside DECO, we release DECO-50 dataset for bimanual dexterous manipulation with tactile sensing, consisting of 50 hours of data and over 5M frames, collected via teleoperation on real dual-arm robots. We train DECO on DECO-50 and conduct extensive real-world evaluation with over 2,000 robot rollouts. Experimental results show that DECO achieves the best performance across all tasks, with a 72.25% average success rate and a 21% improvement over the baseline. Moreover, the tactile adapter brings an additional 10.25% average success rate across all tasks and a 20% gain on complex contact-rich tasks while tuning less than 10% of the model parameters.
